html:
A hymn writer of the 6th century, the great master of the kontakion. He was born at Emesa, today's Homs in Syria, served as a deacon in Beirut and came to Constantinople around the reign of the emperor Anastasius.

A kontakion is a long sermon in verse, sung in church. It has many stanzas of the same pattern, tied together by a refrain, and the first letters of the stanzas often spell a phrase. Romanos used it to retell Bible stories with drama and dialogue. A legend says the Virgin Mary gave him a scroll to eat in a dream, and the next morning he sang his famous Christmas hymn.

Dozens of his works survive. One responds to the Nika riots and the rebuilding of the city's great church by Justinian. He is a saint of the Orthodox Church and a central figure in early Byzantine music.
